entry.name: bitshift~
entry.digest: Bit shifting for floating point signals
entry.description: Use the bitshift~ object to perform bitwise operations on a floating point signal as bits or as an integer.

arguments.name: number-of-bits/direction-of-shift
arguments.digest: Number of bits to be shifted
arguments.description: Sets the number of bits to be shifted on the incoming floating-point signal. Positive shift values correspond to left shifting that number of bits, negative shift values correspond to right shifting that number of bits.

arguments.name: operational-mode
arguments.digest: Processing mode for floating signal/floating-point values
arguments.description: Specifies whether the floating-point signal or floating-point value will be processed as a raw 32-bit floating-point value or converted to an integer value for bit shifting. The modes of operation are listed below.0: Treat floating-point signal input as a raw 32-bit value (default).1: Convert the floating-point signal input to an integer value.

attributes.name: mode
attributes.digest: Processing mode for floating signal/floating-point values
attributes.description: Specifies whether the floating-point signal or floating-point value will be processed as a raw 32-bit floating-point value or converted to an integer value for bit inversion. The modes of operation are listed below.0 - Treat floating-point signal input as a raw 32-bit value (default).1 - Convert the floating-point signal input to an integer value.Note: If you convert the floating-point signal input to an int and then convert it back, the resulting floating-point value will retain only 24 bits of integer resolution.
